newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong to mark China National Day for first time.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to mark China National Day for first time.

text.p: Hong Kong will celebrate China's National Day on October 1 for the first time since the former British colony reverted to Chinese rule, and plans speeches, sports and a spectacular fireworks display.

The government said the day would begin with a flag-raising ceremony at the harbour front promenade of the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, where Britain handed the territory back to China at a midnight ceremony on June 30.

Local government boards would organise sports and recreation activities, and the territory's chief executive, Tung Chee-hwa, would host a reception at the convention in the evening, it said in a statement.
A 30-minute fireworks display in the harbour will round out the day.

While Hong Kong has always celebrated traditional Chinese holidays such as the Lunar New Year and the Mid-Autumn Festival, it did not mark Chinese national holidays during its 156 years as a British colony.
Since the handover, British holidays such as the Queen's Birthday have been dropped from the calendar, although traditional festivals like Easter and Christmas remain.
